known.title: The record rule says that the REST issue-comments endpoint returns comments newest first, but GitHub documents ascending order, so archive and show take the oldest owner record of the first page as the latest
known.locator: Research, Decided record rule (line 17); Steps, row 5 plan_mjs (line 34)
known.summary: The record rule reads the review comments with `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/<issue>/comments`, says that the endpoint returns comments newest first, and lets `archive` read only the first page and stop at the first well-formed code-review record of the owner; `show` uses the same read. The page that the plan cites (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/comments#list-issue-comments) says 'Issue comments are ordered by ascending ID', and a page holds 30 comments by default (`per_page`, max 100). So `archive` takes the oldest owner record: an early `Code-review: pass` wins over a later `fixes-required`, and a record after comment 30 is never read. This breaks the goal of step 5 (refuse a superseded pass). The read must page through every comment and take the last well-formed record.

known.title: Research says that the gh stub already answers any REST `gh api` path from its state file, but at repo_ref it answers only `gh api graphql`, so the comment-based CLI cases fail and test_sync leaves the stub out
known.locator: Research, verbatim-assertions bullet (line 19); Steps, row 7 test_sync, Files (line 36)
known.summary: The bullet says that scripts/tests/fixtures/gh-stub/gh already answers `gh api` calls for any REST path from its state file, so it serves issue comments without a change, and step 7 names only plan-skill-phases.mjs and plan-cli.mjs. At repo_ref the stub handles `api` only for `graphql` (line 147), and every other call ends at `die(`unsupported gh command: ...`)` (last line). So the `gh api repos/.../issues/<n>/comments` call of the new archive and show exits 1 in the stub, and the CLI cases of step 7 cannot test the comment-based archive proof. Step 7 must name the stub and teach it the comments route.

known.title: No step changes github-issue-publication.md, which restates the old landing sentence and which the default-pr-landing assertion pins with the other mirrors
known.summary: The bullet lists four mirrors of the landing sentence 'ensure a non-default branch', and the steps change them. At repo_ref, plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/github-issue-publication.md (line 36) holds the same sentence ('After `Code-review: pass`, the manager runs landing without another prompt: ensure a non-default branch, ...'), and scripts/tests/plan-skill-phases.mjs pins it there: assertion `default-pr-landing` (lines 137-139) lists ISSUE_PUBLICATION (line 23) with the four mirrors. No Files cell names the reference. So the reference keeps the old branch rule against the new implement-start rule, and step 7 cannot make one assertion text match all five files. A step must update the publication reference.

known.title: Step release has the Effect `release`, but the plan runs it without an in-session ask because the settled mode covers it, which the contract forbids
known.locator: Research, Release bullet (line 22); Steps, row 9 release (line 38)
known.summary: The Release bullet says that the settled plan-and-implement mode authorizes step 9 like issue publication, so it runs without another question. Step 9 cuts plan-lifecycle 0.8.0 and pushes a tag, with the Effect `release`. At repo_ref, plan-contract.md (Enforcement boundary, lines 335-337) says that a step with a non-`local` Effect requires in-session `ask` confirmation immediately before execution, and the root AGENTS.md (lines 111-115) repeats it; the settled mode covers only routine issue publication and landing, which stay outside the Steps table. The step must have an ask immediately before it runs (or block when `ask` is unavailable), or leave the plan.
